messages:
Carlos Mendes: Heads-up from a demo with FastServe — they asked for a "LatencyShield" offering for sub-100ms inference on short prompts. Asked whether this should be a separate tier, a billable add-on, or a reserved-only SLA. Thoughts?
Neha Gupta: My vote: start as an add-on (toggle) with explicit commit requirement for SLA. Easier to iterate and doesn't create a broad SKU proliferation.
Avery Kim: Add-on is fine, but we need clear technical boundaries: which models, max seq len, and whether quantized variants qualify. Also define a fallback policy if capacity exhausted.
Jon Park: Finance: to justify the engineering investment, we need projected ARPU uplift and a margin target >=50% at expected utilization. For pilots we can accept 42% with case study clause and 6mo commit.
Carlos Mendes: Neha/Avery — can we sketch launch metrics? Fast numbers we can test in next perf run?
Neha Gupta: Quick draft targets: p50 <= 60ms for <=128 tokens, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 600ms under 95% traffic mix. Cost uplift should be <1.8x for typical gen workloads. Allow one missed SLO/month for pilot.
Avery Kim: Operational reqs: Smart Router flag "latency_shield=true", per-request label for billing and tracing, and an emergency ops override (expires after 30m) with audit log. Need a circuit-breaker when burst > contracted monthly cap.
Carlos Mendes: UX: show as toggle under "Performance features" with inline tooltip explaining commit requirement and billing increments. Also show predicted cost delta on the route page.
Jon Park: Billing specifics: meter on per-minute weighted tokens for this add-on, show invoice preview in Console, and require a 3mo minimum commit to qualify for SLA pricing. Promo allowance down to 42% margin for pilots.
ops_bot: PRD link created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PRD-712 "LatencyShield pilot" owners: @Carlos, @Neha, @Avery. CI checklist seeded.
Avery Kim: Legal asks: include explicit burst policy (max 2.5x monthly commit billed at 2.5x rate), termination clawback if early exit < 3mo (10% remaining value), and case study opt-in for pilots.
Carlos Mendes: Rollout plan proposed: invite-only pilot (3 customers) -> expanded beta (15 customers) -> GA. Each stage requires telemetry pass + billing validation.
Neha Gupta: Observability: need new dashboard panels: latency_shield p50/p95/p99, error rates, per-route cost delta, and a churn risk signal (usage drop after promo ends).
Jon Park: Go-to-market: Sales to target platform teams and real-time product teams. Create promo approval workflow in Stripe dashboard for pilot codes.
Avery Kim: Engineering tasks: 1) router flag and canary path, 2) per-request labels in tracing and billing pipeline, 3) canary perf run w/ 3 workloads, 4) circuit-breaker + ops override UI. I'll create tickets and tag eng-runtime.
Carlos Mendes: Launch checklist (quick): 1) perf scripts + baseline vs shield (Neha), 2) billing meter + invoice mockups (Jon), 3) Console toggle + copy (Design/PM), 4) SLA and contract language draft (Legal), 5) observability dashboards + alerts (Avery/SRE), 6) pilot customer signups (Sales).
Neha Gupta: I'll run perf tests this week and post results in #eng-runtime. If numbers look good, we can start outreach to FastServe and two other customers.
Jon Park: I'll prepare pricing bands and promo playbook. Need to agree floor price that meets margin floors at 50% util.
Avery Kim: Ops caveat: if shield traffic causes downstream model instability, auto-fallback to standard tier must kick in and we should flag impacted requests. Add a rollback playbook to the PRD.
Carlos Mendes: Good. Let's meet Thursday EOD to finalize pricing bands and pilot customer list. Add any missing items here. :raised_hands:
